# Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B) Deep Dive Analysis

Report 021 | Published 2020-05-24 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2020-5-24/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/021.json)

Financial-sector value depends on solvency, fiscal support and rates.

The delayed job recovery, bank earnings decline and fiscal-reflation direction were supported. The expected Treasury yield-control regime failed. Reserve creation is repeatedly confused with bank recapitalization, a material mechanistic error. Berkshire succession risk matched an observed decline, while the post-succession restructuring thesis remains early.

**Coverage:** All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

## Claims

### 021-C01

**Full job recovery will be slow**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | forecast |
| Horizon | post-quarantine recovery |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | US employment |
| Source blocks | 12, 14, 15, 16, 17 |
| Thesis family | covid-recovery-scarring |

Payroll employment did not return to its February 2020 level until July 2022 in the contemporary release. That supports the distinction between a reopening bounce and full recovery. Continued claims are beneficiaries, however, not an exact count of all lost jobs.

**Direction:** Resolved as stated.

**Timing:** Original horizon retained: post-quarantine recovery

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [July 2022 Employment Situation release](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_08052022.htm) | Bureau of Labor Statistics | 2022-08-05 | Verified in the audit

The release reported payroll employment and unemployment rate had returned to February 2020 levels in July 2022. This is a publication-vintage recovery date, not a claim about subsequently revised payroll history.

**Timing:** Original horizon retained: late summer 2020

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

- [About the American Rescue Plan](https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/coronavirus/about-the-american-rescue-plan) | US Treasury | Verified in the audit

Weekly total assets rose from $4.183 trillion on February 12, 2020 to $4.242 trillion March 4 and $6.368 trillion April 15. A brief late-February decline preceded the surge.

### 021-C09

**QE recapitalizes banks through reserves**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Wrong |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | Bank balance sheets |
| Source blocks | 49, 56, 59, 61 |
| Thesis family | qe-reserves-versus-capital |

A market-value exchange of securities for reserves improves liquidity but does not automatically increase equity capital. If the seller is a nonbank, the bank gains a reserve asset and matching deposit liability. Loss absorption requires capital, profits, guarantees or direct recapitalization, not merely a larger reserve balance.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

**Outcome evidence:**

- [How money is created](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/explainers/how-is-money-created) | Bank of England | 2019-10-01 | Verified in the audit

Reserves are electronic central-bank settlement money. Capital is a separate resource that absorbs loan-default losses; both liquidity and capital constraints apply to banks.

Archived BRK-B closes: May 2, 2025 $539.79999; May 5 $512.15002, a 5.12% decline across the succession-announcement weekend. Earnings news was also contemporaneous, so the return is not a causal isolation.
